How each evaluation year was fitted

The 2016 evaluation model was trained on the initial 2010-2015 set. Each later evaluation adds the preceding complete season, so the training window expands by one year; the 2026 model uses 2010-2025. Every evaluation year is fitted separately -- 11 fits in all -- and no evaluation year's outcomes appear in its own fit.

Deltas in this report use model_minus_market_log_loss: race_multinomial_log_loss, where negative is better. That is stated because three delta fields existed in this repository and they did not all point the same way.

Provenance -- the source commit, the config and data digests, the environment and every input this report read by content digest -- is in the technical appendix and in run_lock.json beside this file. Canonical publication fails without it.

Evaluation population and market reference

The market reference

Every metric below is reported beside the market's own implied probabilities on the same races, normalised within each race. The delta is this model's race log loss minus the market's on the same races; negative is better.

The evaluation population

Every figure in this report covers the evaluation window beginning in 2016. 2015 is earlier than the window and is excluded from every evaluation figure below, including the bankroll paths. The feature-effect grid is the one exception, and says so where it appears: a learned response direction is a property of each year's fit rather than of the evaluation population.

Splits present: test, train_apparent, train_prequential. Only the forward test split is scored above. The others exist to be compared against it -- an apparent-fit number looks far better than a forward one -- and are never pooled with it.

Out-of-fold margin sources: market_fallback, model.

One or more years is partial

2026 does not span a full season, so its per-year figures rest on fewer races than the others. Partial years are marked in every table rather than dropped, because dropping them would silently change the evaluation population.

The largest departure is the 0.000 to 0.010 bin, and every stage misses there: market 0.53, raw_offset 0.77, temperature 0.86, market_blend 0.74, bagged 0.75. market is furthest from 1.0 at 0.53, meaning that bin won fewer races than it priced; temperature is closest at 0.86, so this bin is where the pipeline moves calibration most. On the market stage that bin holds 10,687 runners, the 6th smallest of 10 bins, so the departure is not a thin-bin artefact. Calibration in this bin does not improve monotonically through the pipeline: temperature reaches 0.86 and market_blend falls back to 0.74, so that step gives back part of the correction rather than adding to it.

This grid covers every year the run fitted, including any the evaluation population excludes. A learned response direction is a property of that year's fit rather than of the race population the headline metrics are computed on, and its per-feature mean is the stability table's tail_effect exactly -- so restricting one and not the other would have two parts of this report describe different populations. 14 of 27 features keep the same sign in every year they appear in. For the seven features that are constant within a race -- a racecourse, a surface -- the cell is the correction's magnitude and not its direction, because a race-constant feature cancels from every pairwise utility difference and has no direction to report. Which basis a row uses is in its tooltip and in the stability table's curve_basis column. A feature whose row changes colour is not necessarily broken: it may genuinely matter differently in different years. But its mean effect is then a summary of disagreeing years, and the mean is the least informative number about it.

Betting and bankroll analysis

Retrospective odds

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Do not select a threshold from these returns.

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

Expected is the model's mean estimated return. Realised is official payout minus stake, divided by stake. Both are before rebate; rebate-aware sizing can change which bets appear, while credited rebates are reflected in the bankroll paths below. Read the pattern across bands rather than one band, because one winner can move a small group.

A negative-edge bucket appears only under rebate-aware sizing, and only at the larger fractions. That is the rule working as defined rather than a filter failing: the rebate is a cliff, so a runner whose own edge is negative can pay for itself by pushing the race's turnover over the threshold, and the stakes only get large enough for that at the higher fractions.

The 2016 evaluation model was trained on the initial 2010-2015 set. Each later evaluation adds the preceding complete season, so the training window expands by one year; the 2026 model uses 2010-2025. Every evaluation year is fitted separately -- 11 fits in all -- and no evaluation year's outcomes appear in its own fit. Each path is rebased on its own opening balance, so zero means break-even for every line from the same point. These curves are drawn from a bounded 999-point subsequence of up to 3,029 staked races, keeping each interval's highest and lowest balance so no peak or drawdown is smoothed away, and keeping the first and last points exactly. Every figure in the tables is computed from the full settlement, and the complete per-race path is in <code>race_paths.parquet</code>. Where a year is excluded, a continuous path opens at the balance the bank held when the kept years begin and an annual-reset path opens at the declared bankroll, so the two show different opening figures for the same rule. Rebate policy: 10% of the race net loss, once that loss reaches HK$10,000, as a cliff. Flat staking is omitted from these panels. Its stake is a fixed amount per bet and this settlement never halts on ruin, so its path can pass below zero -- a measure of how badly a rule loses rather than a balance an account could hold. It is also not a Kelly fraction, so it belongs to no preset. annual-reset re-settlement of continuous-path decisions: the same stakes, compounded from the declared opening balance at the start of each test year. Not an annual-reset sizing simulation -- stakes are not re-solved from reset capital, and doing so would change which bets are placed rather than only how they compound. Each bankroll scenario below is solved from its own opening balance, sequentially by race, because the rebate threshold is a fixed dollar amount and the fraction the solver sees therefore changes with the bank. The larger scenario is not the smaller one's stakes scaled up. 2015 is excluded from every path below. That year's utility scale fell back to its theoretical value rather than being fitted, so its stakes are not comparable with the rest.

Winners drawn from the model's own probabilities. 9 of 54 settled series shown, filtered to model view bagged_offset.

One simulation was declined rather than approximated

Refusals are recorded rather than omitted, so a reader can see the strategy was considered and declined. Rebate-aware sizing cannot reuse stale bankroll-dependent fractions on a divergent path.

The realised path, the day-block bootstrap and the model-assumed MC answer different questions and must not be shown as one uncertainty band.

What a simulation cannot tell you

The model-assumed simulation draws winners from the model's own probabilities. If those probabilities are wrong the simulation is confidently wrong in the same direction, so it bounds sampling risk and says nothing about model risk.

Limitations and the retrospective-odds warning

Retrospective odds, restated

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Restated at the end as well as beside the betting numbers, deliberately. It is the single most load-bearing caveat in this report and the one a reader skimming for a return figure is most likely to miss.

Every test year is also development data

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

What else this report does not establish

  • It measures Softmax Offset against the market on the evaluated races; it is not a cross-model comparison.
  • Its intervals condition on the fitted model, so they bound sampling risk and not model risk.
  • Every figure is out of sample in time but in sample in design: the feature set, the hyperparameters and the staking rules were all chosen with these years visible.
  • Nothing here is a shadow test. A profitability claim needs a locked model run forward against timestamped pre-race prices.
Unverified source state

This run recorded a dirty source tree, so its numbers cannot be reproduced from the named commit alone.
